title: GPU memory fair-striping and KV prefetch stabilizer
creator: Ava Chen
description: When tenants surge, our current KV prefetch + continuous batching pipeline creates transient spikes in KV and activation memory that cause conservative global evictions and throughput drops. This ticket implements a fairness-oriented memory striping plus a prefetch stabilizer that smooths transient KV/activation demand and preserves weight residency, reducing tail latency and eviction churn.
problem_statement: Observed behavior: short-lived tenant bursts trigger aggressive KV prefetch and large multi-tenant batches. GPU memory for KV + activations spikes, forcing conservative evictions of weight shadow copies or full model slices. Result: higher token latency tail, more cold weight reads, and increased OOM/in-flight request retries for affected tenants. Existing headroom heuristics are binary and reactive; we need a proactive, smoothed approach that preserves QoS across tenants while keeping unit cost low.
proposed_solution: Introduce two coordinated mechanisms: (1) Fair striping of transient KV allocations across a small number of in-GPU reservoirs (stripes) that limit per-tenant burst occupancy and allow predictable eviction windows; (2) A KV prefetch stabilizer that applies EWMA smoothing to prefetch rate triggers and uses adaptive throttles based on per-stripe pressure and batch latency signals. The stabilizer supports speculative prefetch at low confidence but decays quickly when pressure rises. Combine with a light-weight admission policy for continuous batching that prefers batches with similar per-request memory profiles to reduce activation variance.
scope: In-scope: runtime allocator changes for stripe bookkeeping, prefetcher rate controller, admission filter in batcher, telemetry hooks for stripe pressure and eviction events, unit and integration tests, and an experiment run on a single Dedicated capacity pool. Out-of-scope: full multi-region rollout, on-prem packaging changes, and long-term pricing adjustments.
success_metrics: - 30% reduction in 99.9th-percentile token latency for bursty tenant workloads (measured on benchmark harness). - 40% reduction in eviction-induced model reloads during simulated tenant surges. - <1% regression in median latency across stable workloads. - No more than 5% increased GPU utilization relative to baseline for equivalent throughput.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests -> 2) Canary on synthetic dedicated pool (low traffic) with telemetry dashboard -> 3) A/B experiment against baseline for 48h with controlled burst traces -> 4) Gradual ramp to 25% of Dedicated capacity -> 5) Full enablement with toggle and operator knobs (stripe_count, ewma_alpha, prefetch_max_rate). Toggle defaults: off. Prior to enabling broadly, run smoke regression on Console dashboards.
risks: - Incorrect stripe sizing could increase fragmentation and reduce effective weight residency. - Over-aggressive smoothing may under-prefetch, hurting latency for some requests. - Complexity in allocator state could increase GC/CPU overhead. - Interactions with existing KV compression/eviction policies may produce edge-case regressions.
test_plan: Unit tests for stripe allocator invariants, integration tests with synthetic mixed-tenancy traces, load tests reproducing historical burst patterns from telemetry, canary runs with e2e tracing (trace IDs), and a fail-open validation ensuring toggles can be instantly reverted. Bench harness names: memory-fair-stripe-2026 and kv-prefetch-stabilizer-2026.
